list.q: Do you charge by the hour or by the job?
list.a: Both, depending on the work. Small repairs are usually by the job — you get a flat price upfront. Longer or less predictable projects (like a full deck repair where I won't know the extent until I start) are hourly. I'll tell you which applies before I start, always.

list.q: How far in advance do I need to book?
list.a: Usually 3–5 days for non-urgent jobs. If something's an emergency — a broken door that won't lock, a leak — call me and I'll do my best to get there sooner. I work Monday through Saturday so there's usually flexibility.
Yes. I carry general liability insurance and maintain my handyman registration. I'll provide proof before any job if you need it — most people ask, and I understand why.

list.q: Do you do electrical or HVAC work?
list.a: Light fixtures, ceiling fans, outlet covers, switches — yes. Full rewiring or panel work — no, that needs a licensed electrician and I'll tell you so. Same with HVAC: filter swaps and basic stuff yes, compressor work no. I won't take a job I can't do right.

list.q: What if the job turns out to be bigger than expected?
list.a: I call you before I go further. You decide whether to proceed, adjust scope, or stop — no surprise charges on your invoice. I'd rather have that conversation than have you unhappy at the end.
